summary: OpenCollab is a multi-agent coding runtime that declares roles and topologies explicitly, holds tools, budgets and context constant across configurations, and logs fine-grained events. That lets it measure 'Adherence', whether the declared collaboration actually happened, and apply a complier-average-causal-effect (CACE) correction to team-vs-single gains. On 36 SWE-bench Pro tasks, adherence ranges from 47.2% to 97.2% depending on model, tools, budget, role card and topology. A code-driven two-coder workflow (Duo) tops Mini-SWE-agent, Codex CLI and Claude Code, all run with GPT-5.6-Luna, on SWE-bench Pro, Terminal-Bench 2.1 and DeepSWE subsets.

claims.claim: Changing a single configuration dimension moves Adherence from 47.2% to as high as 97.2%.
claims.evidence: Table 3 on 36 tasks with Clopper-Pearson 95% CIs (e.g. Qwen3.8-Flash 47.2 [30.4, 64.5] vs GPT-5.6-Luna 97.2 [85.5, 99.9]; read-only tools 94.4; mandatory card 91.7; ring 91.7). The large shifts have non-overlapping CIs, so the claim is well supported for this one SWE-bench Pro sample.

claims.claim: OpenCollab (Duo) sets new SOTA against mainstream harnesses: 64.25% SWE-bench Pro, 83.15% Terminal-Bench 2.1, 69.91% DeepSWE.
claims.evidence: Table 2 numbers are present, but these are single runs on subsets (193 / 89 / 113 tasks). The SWE-Pro margin over Codex CLI is 64.25 vs 63.73 (1 task), and on Terminal-Bench it is 83.15 vs 80.90 (2 tasks). The authors themselves state that rerunning the single agent flips 5 of 36 tasks. All harnesses use GPT-5.6-Luna, which is non-native for Claude Code (58.03, the lowest on SWE-Pro). Only DeepSWE shows a clear margin.

claims.claim: Collaboration beats working alone: Duo over Base by +3.4 (Terminal-Bench) and +14.2 (DeepSWE).
claims.evidence: Table 9 paired sign tests: DeepSWE 21 vs 5 discordant (p=0.0025); Terminal-Bench 6 vs 3 (p=0.51, not significant, as the authors concede). Duo runs two full solvers plus selection, i.e. best-of-two with a selector, using 2.2x the tokens on DeepSWE (26.11M vs 11.95M). A compute-matched single-agent best-of-2 baseline is missing.

claims.claim: The single-agent configuration uses the fewest tokens across all suites.
claims.evidence: Table 2: Base 3.89M / 1.54M / 11.95M tokens and the lowest cost ($0.41 / $0.19 / $1.19) on all three benchmarks.

claims.claim: Adherence-adjusted CACE allows causal attribution of organizational gains.
claims.evidence: Theory in App. A, but §4.3 undercuts the headline use: under the open card, the +5.6 ITT comes from the 19 non-adherent tasks (+15.8), while the 17 adherent tasks show -5.9, so the +11.8 CACE 'should not be read as the complier effect'. Higher adherence also coincides with lower Pass@1 (read-only 94.4% adherence with 52.8% pass vs 47.2% with 75.0%).

patterns.note: A model-directed team mostly does not collaborate as declared; where it does (high adherence), pass rate often drops. Gains come from a code-scripted Duo workflow, which is closer to parallel sampling plus selection than to role-based teamwork.
Two coders in separate repository copies or candidate environments, with code selecting a patch, gave +14.2 on DeepSWE (p=0.0025). Not significant on Terminal-Bench.
Star topology with an Adopter that 'monopolizes execution until exhausting its token budget' (§4.3) shows orchestrators skipping delegation unless tools force it.
Event streams expose the declared-vs-realized gap that outcome metrics hide, and caught 10 leaked-answer attempts on Terminal-Bench (App. B.1.2).
Per-role token allowances enforced by pre-call gates. The budget ablation shows 0.5M per role cuts Pass@1 to 44.4%.
Tool-set restriction (read-only, no edit) is the strongest lever for forcing delegation.
SWE-bench Pro, Terminal-Bench 2.1 and DeepSWE subsets.

methodology.sample: Adherence experiment: 36 random SWE-bench Pro tasks per configuration. Cross-harness: 193 SWE-bench Pro, 89 Terminal-Bench 2.1, 113 DeepSWE tasks.
methodology.baselines: Mini-SWE-agent, Codex CLI and Claude Code, all driven by GPT-5.6-Luna; plus the authors' single-agent Base. Claude Code with a non-Anthropic model is a weakened configuration. No compute-matched best-of-N single-agent baseline for Duo.
methodology.models: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, Qwen3.8-Flash and GPT-5.6-Luna in the adherence experiment; GPT-5.6-Luna only in the cross-harness comparison.
methodology.variance: Each configuration is run once. Clopper-Pearson CIs on adherence and exact sign tests on paired comparisons. The authors report a rerun-flip rate of 5/36 tasks for the single agent.
methodology.ablations: Single-dimension ablations of model, tools, budget, context card and topology (Table 3).
methodology.contamination_controls: No network in the adherence container. On Terminal-Bench, trajectories were searched for answer leakage and 10 leaked attempts were withdrawn or rerun (App. B.1.2).
methodology.languages: Benchmarks' native mix (SWE-bench Pro and DeepSWE multi-language; Terminal-Bench shell tasks). No per-language breakdown seen.

standards.peer_review: arXiv preprint; comment says 'work on process'.
standards.artifacts: A 'Project page / Code' link is present in the paper (URL not extracted in the text), and App. C.4 says artifacts are 'released with the paper'.

biases.detail: Authors' own runtime, Adherence metric and Duo workflow evaluated by the authors, who also run the competitor harnesses.
Claude Code is run with GPT-5.6-Luna rather than its native models, and nine Claude Code runs were stopped by hand and scored as failed.
Cross-harness Pass@1 comes from single runs; the SOTA margins (1-2 tasks) are inside the 5/36 rerun-flip rate the authors measured.
Adherence and CACE rest on 36 tasks per configuration; benchmarks are subsets.
The cross-harness comparison uses GPT-5.6-Luna only; the limitations section says 'three models, not a model sweep'.
'Establishes new SOTA' over harnesses from 1-2-task margins on subsets.
Duo runs two complete solving processes plus selection at about 1.7-3x the tokens of Base; this is not compared with Base at pass@2 plus the same selector.

coi.affiliations: Mostly Shanghai Jiao Tong University (RISE-X Lab; corresponding author Yihong Dong), plus Cambridge, NTU, HKU, Imperial and Peking University. One author (Xue Jiang) lists Peking University and Tencent.
coi.vendor_products_evaluated: Compares against Anthropic's Claude Code and OpenAI's Codex CLI; no Tencent product evaluated.
coi.funding: No funding statement; acknowledgments thank four contributors only.
coi.detail: Predominantly academic. One vendor-affiliated co-author, with no vendor product judged. The conflict is self-evaluation of their own framework against competitors they configured.

verdict_reason: The adherence analysis (CIs, sign tests, leakage audit, honest CACE caveats) is unusually careful and well supported. The 'new SOTA over Claude Code and Codex' headline is not: single runs, 1-2-task margins, a non-native model for Claude Code, and no compute-matched best-of-2 control for Duo.
applicability: Directly useful for a mixed-host team deciding whether to orchestrate multiple agents. Don't assume a declared multi-agent org actually runs; measure it from traces. A model-directed lead agent often does the work itself unless tool permissions force delegation (read-only orchestrator). The gains that held came from code-scripted parallel candidates in isolated workspaces plus deterministic selection, which maps well to running two agents in separate git worktrees on a spec'd task and picking the patch that passes the shared contract tests across the ≥4 ingestion repos. Budget per role should be at least about 2M tokens before teams pay off. The evidence is Python-heavy benchmark subsets with GPT-5.6-Luna only, and nothing covers Java or cross-repo tasks.

conflicts_with.detail: MSEval reports topology shifting scores by over 30 points. OpenCollab's single-dimension topology ablation moves Pass@1 only 75.0 to 63.9 on 36 tasks, within a measured 5/36 rerun-flip noise floor, and argues such topology comparisons are uninterpretable without verifying adherence.
